items.title: Ontario is restructuring how Peel manages its water services. Critics say it opens the door to privatization — the province disagrees
items.summary: A new publicly-owned corporation is slated to take over water and wastewater services for Brampton, Mississauga and Caledon by 2029. Screenshot taken from Peel region website Advocacy groups are raising concerns about Ontario’s plan to transfer Peel’s water and wastewater services to a publicly-owned corporation, citing fears over reduced public oversight, future privatization and uncertainty over water rates. These concerns stem from the Fighting Delays, Building Faster Act (Bill 60), which began the process of transferring responsibility for Peel’s water and wastewater services from the Region of Peel to Brampton, Caledon and Mississauga. The omnibus legislation enacted the Water and Wastewater Public Corporations Act, 2025, creating a framework for a publicly-owned corporation model to deliver water and wastewater services. Peel was selected as the first jurisdiction to test how the model would function in a large and complex jurisdiction before expanding elsewhere. The transfer to municipalities will commence in 2029, with no specific date designated for when the corporation, which will be jointly owned by the three cities, will begin operating. Representatives from the Brampton Environmental Alliance (BEA) and the Canadian Union of Public Employees (CUPE) argue the new structure could reduce public accountability by shifting decision-making away from elected officials and into the hands of a corporation and its management board.

items.title: Hazel McCallion LRT train will finally get tested on Mississauga streets
items.summary: After years of construction, delays and road disruptions, a real Hazel McCallion Line train is finally preparing to hit the streets of Mississauga. Ontario Transportation Minister Prabmeet Sarkaria said Friday (Aug. 6-billion transit project. “Progress continues on the Hazel McCallion Line, with a light rail vehicle set to begin testing on Topflight Drive in Mississauga next week,” Sarkaria said in a post on X. ” The minister did not provide additional details about the testing, including how long it will continue or exactly how far the train will travel. But the move is significant because the testing is taking place on the actual LRT (light rail transit) corridor rather than being confined to the project’s operations, maintenance and storage facility near Highway 407. It follows the first successful test of a Hazel McCallion Line train under its own power at the facility earlier this year. Metrolinx said in June that the outdoor rail yard’s overhead catenary system had been energized, allowing one of the project’s light rail vehicles to operate under its own power for the first time. The government agency that oversees integrated public transit in southern Ontario, Metrolinx, said at the time that the milestone would pave the way for future vehicle testing on the line.

items.title: House of the week: Upgraded home in family-friendly Mississauga neighbourhood
items.summary: This place: An upgraded home in a family-friendly Mississauga neighbourhood. Features: This upgraded home is located on a corner lot. A grand double-door entry opens to over 4,800 square feet of total living space that features hardwood floors throughout. The main level offers formal living and dining spaces, an office and a family room anchored by a fireplace. The custom kitchen features cabinets, granite countertops and a bright breakfast area overlooking the backyard. The home boasts five bedrooms, including two primary bedrooms. The primary bedrooms have walk-in closets and ensuite bathrooms. The additional bedrooms also have their own closets. The basement features a recreational space. Home updates include a metal roof with a 50-year warranty along with updated windows and window coverings throughout. items.title: Three people charged after 19-year-old driver fatally shot by Toronto police
items.summary: MISSISSAUGA - Toronto police have charged three people, including a teenage girl, alleged to have been in a car with a 19-year-old man who was shot dead by an officer

items.title: Chase That Began Near Toronto's Esplanade Ends With Three Charged in Fatal Mississauga Shooting
items.summary: According to INsauga, Toronto police announced Thursday that three people, including 19-year-old Kahiem Bailey-Whitfield of Mississauga, are facing charges tied to the fatal officer-involved shooting that happened earlier this week near The Collegeway and Winston Churchill Boulevard. Also charged are 23-year-old Naquon Laidley of Toronto and a 17-year-old girl. Police say the case began when officers received a report of a person with a gun near The Esplanade and Lower Jarvis Street in Toronto, and officers from 51 Division identified a suspect vehicle that plainclothes officers then tracked all the way from Toronto into Mississauga. INsauga reports that when officers tried to stop the vehicle near The Collegeway and Winston Churchill Boulevard, the driver attempted to flee and struck a plainclothes officer in the process. What followed, including the shooting that left a man dead, remains under investigation by Ontario's Special Investigations Unit. Bailey-Whitfield now faces multiple firearms charges, including two counts each of possessing a restricted or prohibited firearm without a licence, occupying a motor vehicle with a firearm, possessing a loaded regulated firearm, and possessing a prohibited weapon without authority.

items.title: Port Credit's Waterfront Turns Into a Rib-Eating Marathon This Weekend, With a Midway Attached
items.summary: According to INsauga, Port Credit Ribfest X 2026 takes over Memorial Park from August 7 to 9, marking the second stop in Mississauga this summer for one of Ontario's biggest rib festivals. Produced by Ontario Festival Group and presented by Gelateria Italiana, the three-day event brings in some of North America's top pitmasters serving smoked ribs, pulled pork, brisket, barbecue chicken, smoked sausage and oversized beef “Dino” ribs. INsauga reports the food lineup extends well beyond barbecue, with vendors including Alabama Lemonade, Billy Bob's Bloomin' Onions, Pineapple Queen, Ontario Corn Roasters and BeaverTails rounding out the offerings alongside poutine, roasted corn and other festival staples. Beyond the food, organizers have built out a full weekend of entertainment and activities, including live music, an artisan marketplace, carnival games, a midway, face painting and a dedicated Kids Zone. The entertainment schedule mixes tribute acts with local bands throughout the weekend, and Friday's lineup features Ida-Maria, Dingo, Pink Leather Jackets and Fiddlestix. For anyone looking to spend a summer weekend on the Port Credit waterfront, the festival offers a packed schedule of food and live entertainment through Sunday.

items.title: Credit Valley Conservation Warns of Dangerous Urban Streams as Storms Soak the Region Through Saturday
items.summary: According to INsauga, Credit Valley Conservation issued a flood outlook statement Thursday covering Mississauga, Brampton and Caledon that remains in effect through Sunday. The agency says thunderstorms carrying peak rainfall of 30 to 40 millimetres per hour are possible both Friday and Saturday, with Environment and Climate Change Canada forecasting localized storms across the entire Credit River watershed starting Friday morning and continuing into Saturday evening. CVC reports the upper and middle sections of the watershed had already picked up roughly 20 to 30 millimetres of localized rainfall as of Thursday evening. While the agency says it does not expect the Credit River or its major tributaries to flood outright, it is warning of possible localized flash flooding and water pooling on roads and in low-lying urban areas. CVC cautions that urban streams and rivers can become especially dangerous near culverts, bridges and dams during heavy rain events. Residents are being told to stay away from all watercourses and to keep children and pets clear of moving water through the weekend.
